title: Use #pragma temp pin for observable task outputs in partial Venus DAGs

human_guidance.statement: When a task output is temporarily unused because the DAG is incomplete, and it is not a DAG return value, declare it with #pragma temp pin so it is not reclaimed and remains available for software-versus-RTL comparison.

proposed_rule: In an incremental or deliberately truncated DAG, explicitly list every task output that must be inspected as a Gem5/RTL checkpoint in #pragma temp pin(...) when that output is neither consumed by a downstream task nor declared as a DAG return value.
semantic_effect: The named task-output temporary receives stable exclusive storage in the temporary arena.
Its allocation is not released or reused by normal lifetime-based temporary allocation.
Declaration order determines pin allocation order.
The pragma does not promote the value to a DAG return value, create a dependency, pin a vector register, or change task scheduling.

conditions: the intended downstream DAG is not yet complete or is deliberately cut at the checkpoint
the producer output currently has no consumer
the producer output is not a declared whole-DAG return value
the output must remain observable for bit-exact Gem5-versus-RTL comparison

exclusions_and_costs: Do not use pin merely for an ordinary output whose lifetime is already covered by downstream consumers unless a stable debug address is intentionally required.
Pinning prevents lifetime reuse and can increase temporary-memory peak usage.
Pinning alone does not export bytes to the host; the Gem5/RTL evidence flow must still locate and extract the pinned temporary.

parser.fact: The grammar accepts #pragma temp pin(varlist), requires at least one plain variable name, and rejects pointer spellings.

lifetime_analysis.fact: The interpreter validates pin names as task-output temporaries and records is_pinned plus pin_order.

allocator.fact: Pinned temporaries are bump-allocated in declaration order into an exclusive prefix that normal first-fit lifetime allocation cannot reuse.

implementation_review_required.observation: The current interpreter also implicitly pins every unused task output and every DAG return value. It warns that explicitly pinning such a value is redundant.
implementation_review_required.risk: Relying only on implicit unused-output pinning hides checkpoint intent in BAS and can make behavior dependent on compiler policy. Conversely, documenting explicit pin as mandatory while the compiler calls it redundant is confusing.
implementation_review_required.decision_needed: Review whether explicit checkpoint pin should remain recommended documentation only, suppress the redundant warning for validation checkpoints, or replace implicit unused-output pinning with an explicit contract in a separately approved DSL change.

proposed_foundation_patch.section: BAS temporary observability and #pragma temp pin
required_content: distinction from DAG return values, dependencies, scheduling and vector-register pinning
current implicit-pin behavior and its review status

validation_before_promotion: Compile a focused positive partial DAG with one explicitly pinned, unconsumed, non-return task output and inspect temp_variables.json plus temp_alloc.json.
Prove the checkpoint has a stable address and compare its complete bytes in Gem5 and fresh RTL.
Compile negative cases for an unknown name, an input variable and a pointer spelling and require deterministic rejection.
Compile a memory-pressure case demonstrating that pinning increases or preserves peak temporary usage rather than enabling lifetime reuse.
Decide and test the intended behavior for the current implicit auto-pin and redundant-warning policy.
rollback: Remove the proposed foundation section and this index entry; no DSL, Scheduler, Gem5 or RTL behavior is changed by this proposal.
